items.name: Cowslip
items.text: Pressed in a hymn book in 1931. The hymn was 'All Things Bright and Beautiful', which seems right.

items.name: Dog Rose
items.text: From the hedge by the Halt. Mr Figg swears it flowers when the train is on time. It rarely flowers.

items.name: Harebell
items.text: Fairies' thimbles, Nan Honeysett calls them. She won't pick them. Someone else did.

items.name: Meadow Cranesbill
items.text: Found between the pages of a seed catalogue, marked 'Very nice. Try again next year.'

items.name: Ox-eye Daisy
items.text: Loves me, loves me not. The last petal is missing, so we'll never know.

items.name: Platform Ticket
items.text: One penny to stand on the platform and wave. The best-value ticket on the Great Western.

items.name: Luggage Label
items.text: 'Honeycombe Halt, via Kemble.' The trunk it came off went to Kemble, then Aberdeen, then back.

items.name: Porter's Cap Badge
items.text: Polished by Mr Figg every Sunday evening, whether or not he's wearing the cap.

items.name: Guard's Whistle
items.text: Blow it and every dog in the village sits down. Nobody knows why.

items.name: Hand Lamp
items.text: Red for stop, white for go, green for Mr Figg's cucumber frames.

items.name: First Prize Rosette
items.text: Awarded to Mabel's marrow, 1954. The marrow was later eaten, to general regret.

items.name: Strawberry Jam
items.text: Mrs Pemberton's. Highly commended. She was expecting 'first' and has not forgotten.

items.name: Raffle Ticket
items.text: Number 33011. The prize was a live goose. It was never claimed, and the goose now lives at the pub.

items.name: Coconut
items.text: Won at the coconut shy by the Reverend, who then had no idea how to open it.

items.name: Victoria Sponge
items.text: Jam, cream, a dusting of sugar and forty years of village rivalry.

items.name: Hedgehog
items.text: Card 1 of 5. 'Fond of beetles, slugs and the Colonel's saucer of milk.'

items.name: Brown Hare
items.text: Card 2 of 5. 'Boxes in March and outruns the postman all year round.'

items.name: Kingfisher
items.text: Card 3 of 5. 'A flash of blue under the bridge at Weavers' Row, if you're lucky.'

items.name: Barn Owl
items.text: Card 4 of 5. 'Lives in the church tower. Has never missed Evensong.'

items.name: Dormouse
items.text: Card 5 of 5. 'Sleeps from October to April. Sensible creature.'

items.name: Wold Honey
items.text: Clover, lime and rose. Nan Honeysett's bees have excellent taste.

items.name: Bee Brooch
items.text: A wedding gift to Nan from her Walter, 1901. 'Busy as a bee, sweet as honey,' the card said.

items.name: Beeswax Candle
items.text: Rolled for the Candlemas service. Smells of summer even in February.

items.name: Honey Dipper
items.text: Carved from a fallen branch of the old lime tree by the church.

items.name: Toy Skep
items.text: Woven for a grandchild. The bees were not consulted and remain doubtful.

items.name: Brass Key
items.text: Fits no lock in the village. The Colonel is convinced it opens something important.

items.name: Silver Thimble
items.text: Lost at the Women's Institute in 1948. Found in the Christmas pudding in 1949.

items.name: Pocket Watch
items.text: Stopped at 6:12, the time the milk train is supposed to arrive.

items.name: Best China Teacup
items.text: Only brought out for the vicar, the doctor and the judges.

items.name: Tin Soldier
items.text: Found in the churchyard wall. The Colonel saluted it.
